1981 Inventions\u0000DRV.search:
the drv is a low-to-medium gain overdrive/distortion pedal with a fixed preamp section and a rat-inspired design direction. 1981 inventions describes the drv as its mainstay distortion pedal, while historical reporting identifies a 1985 whiteface proco rat as an important starting point for the design. - **drv:** original model.
- separate modified editions such as **drv2** and **drv mod** are treated as distinct records where documented.
- original drv controls: **drv**, **cut**, and **vol**, plus an on/off footswitch and led. - the archive does not merge drv2 or drv mod component changes into the original drv record.
- no complete production revision chronology was established for the original run. the drv covers clean boost, low-gain overdrive, and more aggressive distortion. the drv and cut controls interact closely, with the cut control shaping the high-frequency content and the drv control increasing gain and perceived low end.

1981 Inventions\u0000DRV MOD 1.search:
the drv mod 1 (white) is the original v1 configuration of 1981 inventions' drv circuit, presented in a white finish and described by the builder as a particularly rare, prototype-era configuration. the current builder documentation describes it as a nuanced distortion designed with jon ashley of bondi effects. [1] - original v1 drv circuit configuration. [1]
- the current edition uses an **opa2134** op-amp and also includes the original op-amp on a socket for component swapping. [1]
- the builder describes a zero-gain mode in which the drv stage is largely removed from the signal path, leaving the preamp section active. [1]
- exact supporting transistor and diode part numbers are not established in the reviewed public documentation. - **drv mod 1 (white)** is identified by the builder as the original configuration for the circuit and technically a prototype-era version. [1]
- the archive does not infer a broader numbered revision history from this single product page. the builder specifically distinguishes mod 1 as the original v1 configuration and describes its zero-gain mode and opa2134 implementation. a complete component-by-component history across all drv variants is not established here. [1] 1981 inventions describes this configuration as a highly nuanced distortion with a clear, thicker preamp character. with the drv control at minimum, the zero-gain mode produces a dark, clean and thick boost-like sound; turning drv up moves the circuit toward warmer, thicker distortion with more normal operation. [1]

1981 Inventions\u0000DRV MOD 2.search:
drv mod 2 is a modified drv distortion circuit with a substantially larger input capacitor for additional low end and a hybrid clipping section combining bat41 and led clipping. 1981 inventions describes the result as warmer, louder and more aggressive than the standard circuit. [1] - drv/cut control layout follows the underlying drv platform. [1]
- larger input capacitor increases low-end content.
- hybrid clipping uses **bat41 diode** and **led** clipping. [1]
- internal switch can select true-bypass operation. [1]
- 9v or 18v standard pedal power is documented for this version. [1] - **drv mod 2 teal** is a documented presentation of mod 2. [1]
- the mod 2 circuit is positioned by the builder between the standard drv circuit and its bass-oriented modification. [1] the defining mod 2 changes are the larger input capacitor and hybrid bat41/led clipping arrangement. the builder describes the version as having more low-end thump, more aggression and a somewhat less tight low end on palm mutes than the standard drv. [1] the builder describes mod 2 as huge, warm, loud and punchy, with more midrange grit than the led-only clipping arrangement. it has substantial low-end thump, can clean up at low gain, and becomes increasingly aggressive as gain rises, reaching textures approaching fuzz. [1]

[1] no numbered factory hardware revision was verified in the archive evidence. the parent identity is therefore retained as a single model. the toor is heavily inspired by a very particular version of the big muff pi pedal made famous by the smashing pumpkins, but that’s about where the similarities end. this does not come at the loss of character of the fuzz tone, as the pedal still retains a raspy clarity to every note.
with enough gain on tap to make even the smallest amp fill a stadium, you’ll be smiling from the moment you engage the footswitch!
the classic scooped midrange of the 90s is still there in its sonic (youth) glory, but my version reinstates the mids to give a full frequency spectrum to your tone.

Abominable Electronics\u0000Cat Dirt Min.search: cat dirt mini is a compact **jfet-based boost** that can also add a little dirt or overdrive. abominable's current catalog lists cat dirt mini as a production pedal, while surviving product descriptions identify the circuit as a sparkle-oriented boost with a small amount of gain available. [1][2] the documented difference for this archive entry is artwork rather than a new circuit. no numbered cat dirt mini hardware revision was verified. cat dirt mini is primarily a clean-to-lightly-dirty boost, with a little extra sparkle and output rather than the thick saturation of a dedicated distortion pedal. pushed harder, it can add a modest amount of overdrive while still behaving more like a tone-and-level enhancer than a full fuzz or distortion box. [2]

Abominable Electronics\u0000Demon Lung.search: demon lung is based on the **boss fz-2 hyper fuzz** and provides two switchable fuzz modes for changing the sound during performance. abominable says the 2020 redesign changed the artwork and moved the pedal to a vertical enclosure while adding a mids control and soft-touch relay switching for the fuzz-mode footswitch. [1] the 2020 redesign is a documented hardware/control change, not just a new artwork treatment. the added mids control and updated switching are the clearest production changes in the available record. [1] demon lung is aimed at the dense, aggressive side of fuzz, with two fuzz modes giving contrasting versions of the fz-2-inspired voice. the added mids control on the later version makes it easier to keep the huge, heavy fuzz audible rather than letting it disappear into a deep mid scoop. [1]

Abominable Electronics\u0000Hail Satan.search: hail satan is abominable electronics' heavily modified big muff-style fuzz/distortion. the builder added a mids control and a second footswitch that changes the clipping from the standard **silicon diodes** to **5 mm red led diodes**, making the alternate mode louder and crunchier. [1][2] the core documented feature set is stable across the standard hail satan family, while artwork and special-edition enclosure treatments vary. the key circuit feature is the switchable silicon-versus-red-led clipping. [1][3] hail satan takes the thick muff-style wall of fuzz and pushes it toward a rougher, crunchier voice with more mids available. the red-led mode is louder and more aggressive than the standard silicon clipping, making the second footswitch function as a tonal and gain jump rather than simply an on/off feature. [1][2]

Abominable Electronics\u0000Hail Satan D.search: hail satan deluxe keeps the original hail satan concept and adds much more control. abominable documents highs, a clean blend, a switch between the original and russian versions, and a dry-signal buffer switch, while retaining the mids, tone, sustain and dirt controls plus the red-led clipping footswitch. [1] the major deluxe evolution is documented through switching improvements and cosmetic updates, while the basic expanded control set remains the identity of the model. the russian/normal switch and clean blend are part of the deluxe design rather than separate versions. [1] the deluxe is designed to make the muff-style foundation considerably more adjustable, from deep and scooped to mid-forward and cutting. the clean blend helps preserve the dry signal while the highs and mids controls shape the upper and middle frequencies, and the normal/russian switch gives two broad voicing families from the same box. [1][2]

Abominable Electronics\u0000Hellmouth.search: hellmouth starts with the classic green tube screamer/ts9-style overdrive and changes the circuit to keep more low end and offer substantially more gain. abominable also adds a clean blend, an input-cap switch, a more-gain switch, and a second footswitch that changes the clipping from stock silicon diodes to red leds. [1][2] the model evolved from the earlier hellmouth into the current four-knob version with a clean control, updated switching and top-mounted jacks. the main circuit concept remained the same: a modified ts-style overdrive with more low end and more gain. [1][2] hellmouth keeps the familiar mid-focused feel of a green tube screamer but adds more low end and much more gain, letting it reach from punchy overdrive into thicker distortion. the clipping switch adds a louder, rougher led mode, while the clean blend can retain some of the dry guitar to keep the heavier settings clearer. [1][2]

Abominable Electronics\u0000Oppressive C.search: oppressive cult destroyer is tuned for bass as well as guitar and is designed to move from subtle overdrive through crunch into heavier distortion. the circuit uses a charge pump to run internally at a higher voltage and adds boost, bass and switchable clipping features around the core drive circuit. [1][2] the pedal gained a clean blend and updated switching/artwork in later production, while its bass-friendly high-headroom design remained intact. earlier documentation specifically identifies mosfet clipping with an added klon-style germanium diode and an alternate led clipping mode. [1][2] oppressive cult destroyer is built to stay thick and controlled on bass while still working on guitar, with enough headroom to keep low frequencies from turning to mush. the boost, bass and clipping controls can move it from comparatively restrained drive into a much louder, harder-edged distortion voice. [1][2]

Abominable Electronics\u0000Throne Torch.search: throne torcher began as a request for an hm-2 clone that could lose some of the original pedal's harshness. abominable added a mids control, switchable led clipping and an additional germanium-diode clipping network, making the pedal capable of both dense hm-2-style grind and thicker boosted textures. [1][2] the later version added clean blend and modernized the switching while preserving the hm-2-based core. the clipping footswitch remains an important part of the design because it provides both a tonal change and a volume/thickness boost. [2] throne torcher delivers the familiar dense, saturated hm-2-style grind but adds more control over the mids and a clipping switch that can fatten the normally thin chainsaw tone. the later clean blend makes it easier to mix the dry signal back in for punch and clarity. [1][2]

Abominable Electronics\u0000Toke Machine.search: toke machine is a very thick, loud fuzz with three primary controls and a second footswitch for a vintage-style octave-up overtone. a destroy toggle adds diode clipping for more volume and intensity, while the current version uses relay-based soft-touch switching. [1] the clearest documented change is cosmetic artwork, while later production uses relay soft-touch switching. no numbered circuit revision was verified. toke machine is voiced for a huge, thick fuzz sound with an overtone-rich octave-up mode that can make lead lines jump out. the destroy function adds extra clipping and volume, pushing the already-heavy fuzz toward a louder, more compressed and aggressive texture. [1]

Abominable Electronics\u0000Yeti Fuzz.search: yeti fuzz is abominable's take on 1960s germanium transistor fuzzes. the builder specifically says the circuit uses a pair of selected nos germanium transistors and a charge-pump voltage inverter so it can run from a normal center-negative 9v supply. [1] no reliable numbered hardware revision sequence was found. the surviving record points to component selection and enclosure finish as part of the pedal's identity rather than a documented v1/v2 circuit split. yeti fuzz is aimed squarely at the soft, harmonically rich feel of vintage germanium fuzzes rather than the harder edge of modern silicon circuits. the selected transistor pair and vintage-style parts support a touch-sensitive, singing fuzz response that can clean up as the guitar level is reduced. [1]

AC Efectos\u0000Green 808 Overdrive.search: green 808 overdrive is an ac efectos overdrive documented by effects database as part of the builder's 2011 catalog entry. the model name and surviving imagery point directly to the classic green 808-style overdrive family. [1][2] no reliable numbered hardware revision sequence was found. green 808 is built around the familiar narrow, mid-forward overdrive approach associated with 808-style pedals. the three-control format keeps it focused on drive amount, tone and output, making it suited to tightening an amp or adding a controlled layer of breakup. [1][2]

AC Efectos\u0000Triplex Distortion.search: triplex distortion is one of the two ac efectos dirt pedals documented in the builder's 2011 introduction. effects database confirms it as a distortion pedal and surviving photography shows volume, sweep and distortion controls. [1][2] no reliable numbered production revision sequence was found. triplex is a simple three-control distortion with sweep providing the main tonal shaping beyond output and distortion amount. the surviving documentation does not provide enough circuit detail to make a more specific lineage claim without guessing, so the archive keeps the description centered on its documented controls and straightforward distortion role. [1][2]

AC Noises\u0000Arpiona.search: arpiona contains three independent effect sections and five circuits, with up to 30 combinations. the octa-synth provides -2, -1 and +1 octave controls; the fuzz adds bass boost and hold-to-oscillate behavior; the boost provides up to +25 db and a noise switch. [1][2] gated, aggressive fuzz can be combined with sub-octave and octave-up synth tones, then pushed by the boost. the hold-to-oscillate function and noise filtering make it capable of unstable, synth-like and noise-oriented textures. [1][2]

AC Noises\u0000Combatti.search: combatti uses an lm308n and offers three clipping modes: open/dynamic, compressed mid-cut, and a more aggressive low-end-defined mode. lowering the distortion control can move it into warm overdrive territory. [1][2] the middle clipping position is open and dynamic, while the upper mode is more compressed and mid-scooped. the lower mode emphasizes defined low end and heavier rhythm textures, with maximum drive entering gritty/fuzz-like territory. [1][2]

AC Noises\u0000Esplora.search: esplora is a silicon-transistor fuzz with level, tone and fuzz controls. one switch can bypass the tone control for a full, mid-heavy voice; the other adds treble brightness and a more aggressive edge. [1][2] the core sound is classic silicon fuzz, but the tone-bypass switch makes it much fuller and more mid-forward. the second switch adds treble presence for a brighter, more cutting fuzz voice. [1][2]

AC Noises\u0000Urla.search: urla combines a cmos fuzz with a dual resonant filter. ac noises describes the fuzz as a digital-logic cmos circuit with a square-wave output and a jfet-based blend control, followed by a dual high-pass/low-pass resonant filter modeled on the korg ms-20. stars music independently confirms the same signal-chain architecture, expression-pedal filter control, relay true bypass, and 9v center-negative operation. [1][2][3] urla is aggressive, gated and experimental, with the cmos fuzz feeding a resonant synth-style filter. it can move from harsh fuzz into sweeping, unstable and highly filtered textures, especially when the filter is controlled externally. [1][2]

AC Noises\u0000Vola.search: vola is a transparent, dynamic overdrive that can also work as a clean boost or preamp. its range goes from subtle signal enhancement to denser overdrive for chords and clear solos. [1][2] vola is touch-responsive and transparent, adding clarity and presence without heavily rewriting the guitar/amp character. higher drive settings become denser while retaining an articulate response. [1][2]

Accel Audio\u0000Vintage Scream'in Overd.search: accel's vintage scream'in overdrive is an analog overdrive voiced for natural, tube-like "scream'in" tones. its three-position toggle selects normal, bright or warm. [1][2] the three modes shift the response between the core overdrive, a brighter/punchier voice and a fuller/warm voice. the pedal is intended to retain a natural, amp-like overdrive feel rather than a heavily saturated distortion character. [1][2]

Acid Age Electronics\u0000Acid Pig - LM3.search: acid pig is a boutique lm308-based rat-style distortion. premier guitar documents selectable silicon, silicon+led and diode-bypassed clipping, plus an overdrive/distortion mode switch. [1] acid pig covers chunky overdrive through saturated rat-style distortion, with the clipping switch changing compression and output character. the led-assisted and diode-bypass positions provide louder/rawer alternatives to the classic silicon clipping voice. [1]

Acid Fuzz\u0000Acid Fuzzer MkI.search: acid fuzz's acid fuzzer mki is a recreation of the 1965 tone bender mki family, with period-style point-to-point construction and selected germanium transistor sets. the builder produced multiple enclosure formats and limited vintage series runs. [1][2] the documented differences are mainly enclosure format and selected germanium transistor sets. the builder keeps the mki circuit identity while changing physical format and transistor sourcing across runs. [1][2] the mki voice is gated, raspy and cutting, with strong attack response and a distinctive sputtering character as the gain/bias is manipulated. the documented builds are designed for aggressive early-tone-bender-style fuzz rather than smooth modern saturation. [1][2]

Acid Fuzz\u0000Italian Fuzz.search: the acid fuzz 1966 italian is a faithful clone of the 1966 production vox tone bender. effects database documents a hand-built circuit loaded with a matched mullard oc76 germanium transistor pair and an adjustable bias control. the current acid fuzz catalog also offers an italian fuzz compact and a limited, numbered vintage series. [1][2] the current compact adds a smaller pedalboard-oriented format and explicit tone-voicing control compared with the earlier documented 1966 italian format. the vintage series is the limited/numbered presentation. [1][2][3] the circuit is intended to deliver the thick, vocal, mid-forward character of the 1966 italian vox tone bender. the adjustable bias can move the fuzz from stable vintage saturation toward sputtery, dying-battery and chainsaw-like textures. [1][4]

Acid Fuzz\u0000Mk1.5.search: acid fuzz describes the mk1.5 as a faithful clone of the 1965 sola sound mk1.5 tone bender. it is extremely close in design to an arbiter fuzz face, with the key documented distinction being its use of oc75 germanium transistors. [1] the mk1.5 occupies the two-transistor tone bender/fuzz face family, with a strong vintage fuzz character and cleanup associated with that topology. the oc75 pair is selected to reproduce the classic 1960s response. [1]

Acid Fuzz\u0000NKT275 Acid Fuzz Face.search: the original limited acid fuzz nkt275 fuzz face used a newmarket nkt275 germanium transistor pair, an internal bias trimmer, and a volume control that also functions as the power switch. the current limited “teardrop” edition continues the original-style enclosure and circuit concept with nos newmarket nkt275 devices. [1][2] the current teardrop edition is a later limited presentation. the original listing documents an older limited run with a wacky old film input capacitor and philips capacitors, while the current edition specifies nos philips “chicklet” and “mustard” capacitors and nos newmarket nkt275s. [1][2] this is the classic two-transistor fuzz face family: thick, blooming fuzz with a strong cleanup response as the guitar volume is reduced. bias adjustment on the original production can push the circuit toward more unstable or sputtery textures. [1]

Acid Fuzz\u0000Professional MkII.search: the professional mkii is a recreation of the 1960s professional mkii tone bender. acid fuzz documents hand-selected germanium transistors, adjustable bias, a tone switch, and a built-in power isolation arrangement. documented transistor options include mullard oc75, oc81d and ac125 devices depending on build. [1] the mkii mini is a smaller, pedalboard-friendly version with optional external bias and additional build options. the original professional mkii format is the larger vintage-style recreation with its built-in controls and component options. [1][3] the professional mkii is voiced for thick, smooth, highly sustaining tone bender fuzz with a characteristic germanium edge. the bias control can move it from the centered vintage voice toward sputtery, dying-battery and chainsaw-like textures, while the tone switch can thin the low/mid content for more cutting lead and rhythm placement. [1]

Acid Fuzz\u0000Selmer Buzz Tone.search: the original selmer buzz tone is a british late-1960s fuzz with two controls, depth and volume, and an unusual low-voltage power arrangement. acid fuzz describes its version as an exact replica and specifically says it uses the original trio of three rca 2n2613 germanium transistors. acid fuzz also describes the circuit as a dirty full-range booster rather than a conventional fuzz, despite cataloging it in the fuzz section. [1][2] the re-build is a separate construction variant rather than simply a cosmetic revision. it retains the original eyelet-board layout but adds modern true-bypass switching and an led, while the main buzz tone recreation is wired in a more original-style format with a fixed input cable and integrated on/off switch. [1][4] this is a loud, wide-range, amp-pushing dirt box with a strong vintage transistor character rather than a conventional woolly fuzz. acid fuzz describes it as adding amp-like coloration and enough output to push an amplifier hard, while the depth control changes the intensity and character of the dirt. [1]

Acid Fuzz\u0000Sonic Boom.search: sonic boom is a three-effect analog unit based on the vox onboard effects circuit. it combines a frequency-selective booster, a germanium or silicon fuzz/distortion section depending on build, and a highly modified vox repeat percussion-style repeater. acid fuzz produced both point-to-point and pcb construction, with later versions adding more routing, voicing, and control options. [1][2] the major changes are construction and transistor flavor. the p2p version is the original hand-wired format, while the pcb version moved the same basic circuit into a more production-friendly build. germanium and silicon versions change the fuzz/boost transistor character, while later pcb revisions expanded routing and repeater controls. [1][2][3] sonic boom is less a single fuzz sound than a small psychedelic effects rig in a box. the fuzz can get aggressive and saturated, the booster can either slam the fuzz for more gain or precede it for a filtered, parked-wah-like character, and the repeater ranges from choppy tremolo into more extreme ring-mod-like territory. [2]

Acid Fuzz\u0000The Zoink Machine.search: the zoink machine is a smaller, pedalboard-friendly zonk machine clone. its core circuit uses a trio of nos 1960s germanium transistors and is deliberately tuned for a clear, articulate fuzz that keeps individual notes audible in chords and fast lead playing. [1][2] the core zoink design stays tied to the zonk machine circuit, while the documented dbii tuning changes the feel and cleanup response for doyle bramhall ii. the tone switch also broadens the usable range beyond the very bright original-style middle position. [1][3] the zoink is tight, articulate and unusually good at keeping chords intelligible for a vintage-style germanium fuzz. the standard voicing is bright and cutting, while the tone switch can add mids or open the frequency range; the dbii tuning pushes the response toward a more gated, pinched-note character. [1][3]

Acid Fuzz\u0000Zonk Machine - Vintage Se.search: this is the larger vintage-style acid fuzz zonk machine rebuild, designed to reproduce the aggressive and dynamic character of an original mid-1960s zonk machine while retaining sensitivity to playing dynamics. acid fuzz documents a hand-selected trio of nos germanium transistors and vintage-style capacitors. [1][2] this is the limited vintage series reconstruction rather than the smaller zoink machine. it keeps the larger original-style format and a specific transistor trio, while the zoink was developed later as a more compact pedalboard version with additional tone shaping and tuning options. [1][3] the vintage series zonk is designed to be aggressive, dynamic and highly responsive to picking strength. it retains the raw attack and expressive cleanup associated with the original zonk machine rather than smoothing the circuit into a modern high-gain fuzz. [1]

Aclam Guitars\u0000Cinnamon Drive.search: cinnamon drive is an original aclam circuit designed from the ground up around the feel of pushed 1960s and 1970s british tube amps. aclam describes a combination of soft and hard clipping stages with cascading gain that lets the pedal move from clean preamp sounds through overdrive into heavy saturation. no numbered hardware revision was documented in the official material reviewed. the product identity is the original cinnamon drive dual-stage design. cinnamon drive starts around clean boost and low-gain overdrive, then adds a second gain stage for thicker and more saturated distortion. the cascading stages and soft/hard clipping are intended to keep the response dynamic and amp-like rather than turning every setting into the same block of gain. [1]

Aclam Guitars\u0000Cinnamon Drive - Drea.search: the dreamer edition uses the cinnamon drive platform, with aclam describing the same dual-stage clipping approach, dynamic response and broad range from overdrive into distortion. the official dreamer product page lists the same core cinnamon drive feature set and power requirements. [1] no circuit change was documented on the official dreamer product page reviewed. it is treated as a named edition of the cinnamon drive platform rather than a newly numbered circuit revision. [1] the dreamer edition is built around the cinnamon drive's flexible, amp-like response, moving from clean boost and lighter overdrive into thicker distortion. the core design emphasizes dynamics and natural-feeling clipping instead of a fixed one-voice drive sound. [1]

Aclam Guitars\u0000Dr. Robert.search: dr. robert is designed around the distinctive preamp/distortion character of the 1966 vox ul730. aclam specifically based the design on its own 1966 ul730, serial number 3042, to bring that unusual british solid-state amp voice into a compact pedal format. [1] aclam states that v3 keeps the sound and character of earlier dr. robert versions while making the pedal more versatile. the important documented change is that bass, treble and mach schau gain controls that were previously internal are now on the front panel, and v3 adds a global lo/hi gain mode. [1] dr. robert is aimed at the unusual, compressed and gritty character of the vox ul730 rather than a generic modern distortion voice. aclam's current v3 keeps that vintage british coloration while expanding the control range and gain options. [1]

Aclam Guitars\u0000Go Rocky Go.search: go rocky go is a faithful recreation of the brilliant channel of aclam's vox conqueror s/n 2004. it recreates the clean preamp character, the built-in fuzzy distortion and the original mid-range boost, then adds a separate crunch mode for a lower-gain voice. [1] the standard go rocky go is the base production model. the later white album edition is documented by aclam as the same circuit with a special finish and was initially produced as 68 individually numbered pieces. [2] the clean mode keeps the character of the vox conqueror preamp, while the distortion mode delivers the original amp's fuzzy vintage breakup. the m.r.b. boosts selectable mid frequencies, and the added crunch mode sits between clean and distortion, giving the pedal a broader range than the original circuit alone. [1]

Aclam Guitars\u0000Go Rocky Go - White A.search: the white album edition is aclam's special-edition version of go rocky go. aclam states directly that it shares exactly the same circuit as the original go rocky go and that the change is the exclusive finish. [1] aclam explicitly states that the white album edition does **not** change the circuit or sound. the distinguishing change is the exclusive finish, with the first run limited to 68 individually numbered units. [1] because aclam states the circuit is unchanged, the white album edition has the same clean, fuzzy distortion, mid-boost and added crunch range as the standard go rocky go. the special edition changes the visual presentation rather than the way the circuit sounds. [1]

Aclam Guitars\u0000The Mocker.search: the mocker is based on the built-in fuzz circuit of aclam's own 1966 vox ul730 s/n 3042. aclam says a component in the original amp had drifted out of specification and produced a gated, spluttery response, so that behavior was deliberately preserved and made adjustable with a bias control. [1] the documented production change is primarily enclosure-related after the original 200-unit run. aclam states that the later version still uses genuine nos philips oa200 diodes and that the electronics and sound remain unchanged. [1] the mocker can be biased from the original amp's gated, spluttery character toward a more open 1966 fuzz response, with the bias control also taking it into other textures. the tone control broadens the usable range across different guitars and rigs, while the circuit remains centered on the distinctive ul730 fuzz character. [1]

Aclam Guitars\u0000The Windmiller Preamp.search: the windmiller preamp is based on aclam's own grampian reverberation type unit 636 s/n 1138. aclam kept the distinctive preamp character but developed the pedal for modern use with a substantially improved signal-to-noise ratio, added treble response and simple high/low-cut tone shaping. [1] the major documented development change was a move away from the early overdrive concept toward a dedicated grampian 636 preamp. aclam also added noise reduction and two simple cut controls to make the pedal quieter and easier to fine-tune while keeping the basic character of the original circuit. [2] the windmiller can operate as a clean boost or as a gritty preamp that pushes an amp or another drive harder. its two cut controls let the player trim low and high frequencies around the core grampian-style character, making it useful for both cleaner boost duties and rawer overdriven sounds. [1][2]

Aclam Guitars\u0000The Woman Tone.search: the woman tone combines a custom humbucker pickup simulation circuit with a touch-sensitive plexi-inspired overdrive using discrete components. a dedicated woman mode footswitch activates the woman tone shaping, making the clapton-style frequency emphasis available without reaching for the guitar's tone control. [1][2] a 2022 guitarist review documents an internal dip switch for a darker tone-capacitor setting and a woman mode footswitch that engages the woman tone control while slightly increasing gain and low end. the current aclam store description still documents the same core pickup-simulation and woman tone concept, but a specific circuit change tied to ap0040 versus ap0120 was not verified. [1][2] the woman tone is voiced around a rounded, sustaining cream-era overdrive with a simulated vintage humbucker response feeding a plexi-style drive. its dedicated woman mode shifts the tonal balance toward the darker, vocal-like character associated with clapton's cream-era setup while retaining a usable overdrive range outside the preset. [1][2]

Acorn Amps\u0000Epstein Didn't Kill Hims.search: the epstein didn't kill himself fuzz is a three-transistor silicon fuzz designed around a simple volume and fuzz control scheme. acorn's current product page describes a range from gritty boost to heavy fuzz crunch, with a separate toggle controlling the illuminated “n't” section of the front-panel lettering. [1] no documented circuit revision history was found in the production material reviewed. the current official image filename includes “v2,” but the product page does not document a specific electronic change, so that filename alone is not treated as a verified hardware version. [1] the pedal moves from lightly dirty boost into heavier, fuzzier crunch as the fuzzy recollection control is advanced. acorn says its voicing is sonically similar to the discontinued bweep fuzz, keeping the effect in a direct, aggressive fuzz family. [1]

Acorn Amps\u0000Kakarot Fuzz.search: kakarot fuzz uses one germanium transistor feeding one silicon transistor, followed by a pair of leds for an additional clipping section. acorn describes the fuzz control as sweeping the pedal from gritty boost territory into fuzz crunch. [1] no separate electronic revision was documented. the current official page presents original and blue as color options of the same kakarot fuzz circuit. [1] the kakarot moves from gritty boost into increasingly fuzzy and compressed sounds as the fuzz control is advanced. the extra led clipping section adds another clipping stage beyond the two-transistor core, helping the pedal cover more aggressive textures. [1]

Acorn Amps\u0000Mind Killer Dual Distort.search: mind killer contains two separate distortion circuits wired in series, each independently switchable and each equipped with its own bass-boost and clipping-mode toggle switches. acorn identifies both sides as single-op-amp distortion circuits. [1] no separate named production revision was documented in the official material reviewed. each side can be used alone or stacked with the other, moving from individual crunchy distortion voices into much denser, higher-gain combinations. the bass and clipping options let each side change character before the two are combined. tightfuzz was amptweaker's 2012 response to requests for a more controllable classic transistor fuzz. it combines a fuzz face-style transistor section with amptweaker's tight low-cut/attack control, auto-biasing fuzz control, selectable germanium/silicon output stage, 60s/70s voicing, edge/smooth shaping, and a pre/post effects loop. [6] tightfuzz combines vintage fuzz face-style behavior with unusually modern control over the low end and attack. the germanium setting is softer and lower gain while silicon is brighter and higher gain; the auto-biasing fuzz control allows the range to move from unusually clean boost-like territory into heavy fuzz, and the edge/smooth and 60s/70s controls move the texture from sharper/tighter to thicker and smoother. DLS Effect\u0000Reckless Driver.search:
the reckless driver is a two-channel analog drive pedal that dls describes as a **distortion/overdrive**. its normal and boost channels each have independent volume, gain, and clean-mix controls, with the normal stage feeding the boost stage. dls created the design in 2013 after dealers asked the company to develop an overdrive, and the pedal was formally announced in february 2014.

the archive keeps the catalog classification as **overdrive** because that is the canonical record identity, while the manufacturer and manual explicitly describe the circuit as covering both overdrive and distortion. the original reckless driver documentation establishes:
- **normal volume, gain, mix:** sets the normal channel's output, drive, and clean-signal blend.
- **boost volume, gain, mix:** sets the boost channel's output, drive, and clean-signal blend.
- **bass:** full-range bass control with dynamic response.
- **treble:** wide-range treble control with dynamic response.
- **attack:** two-position voicing control. right/high-attack adds a little more attack and brightness; left is warmer and smoother.
- **boost footswitch:** selects the boost channel. dls notes that the boost selector can be switched even while the effect itself is bypassed.
- **on/off footswitch:** true-bypass effect switching.

dls explains that the normal channel drives the boost channel, so the boost volume behaves in relation to the normal channel's level in a way the company compares to a master-volume relationship. dls' original datasheet documents an **internal voltage charge pump that raises the operating voltage to about 13v** for higher headroom and a clear but warm overdrive/distortion response.

the enclosure contains two internal adjustments:
- **input-stage / drive gain pot:** clockwise increases gain.
- **rt2 distortion-input-stage pot:** counterclockwise gives more distortion, bite, and straight-drive character; clockwise gives less distortion and a smoother drive.

dls specifies high-quality 1/4-inch amphenol input and output jacks, a die-cast aluminum enclosure, and a 3p3t true-bypass switch.

no exact production transistor or semiconductor part number is identified in the model-specific documents reviewed for this pass. dls positions the pedal as covering clean boost, overdrive, and more aggressive distortion by combining the channel gain and clean-mix controls.

in its 2014 review, premier guitar found the normal channel capable of low-to-mid-gain, edge-of-breakup sounds and described the pedal as strongly touch-sensitive. the review reported that harder picking increased the perceived rasp of the overdrive while lighter playing produced a smoother response. with both stages driven hard, the reviewer described the distortion as aggressive but still articulate, with useful note definition and picking dynamics.

premier guitar also reported that the attack switch changes the feel and brightness of the response and that the shared bass/treble section gives substantial control over how the pedal interacts with different amplifiers. those are review observations, not claims of an objectively fixed frequency response.

DOD Electronics\u0000Bass Overdrive (FX9.search:
the **dod fx91 bass overdrive** is an analog bass-focused overdrive/distortion pedal introduced at **winter namm 1998**. dod's manual describes it as a distortion box designed specifically for bass that lets the player blend the processed signal with the original clean bass signal. effects database lists the same four-control layout and identifies the model as an overdrive.

the design is closely related to the contemporary **fx102 mystic blues overdrive**. collector research and circuit documentation identify the fx91 as sharing the same basic circuit family, modified for bass voicing and the low-end requirements of the instrument. the documented control set is:
- **level:** overall output level.
- **blend:** mixes the clean bass signal with the driven signal.
- **tone:** post-distortion high-frequency eq.
- **drive:** controls gain in the distortion stage.

the blend control is the important functional feature of the design. it allows the distorted signal to be mixed back with the unaffected bass signal so the player can add grind while retaining the instrument's fundamental low-end presence. americaspedals identifies **two 4560-type op-amps** in the fx91 and notes an example component-side circuit-board photograph from **april 2000, revision b**. the same source identifies the fx91 as sharing its basic circuit with the fx102 mystic blues overdrive.

a 2014 circuit-analysis write-up describes the signal path as an input buffer feeding a conventional clipping amplifier, followed by the blend mixer, then a tone stage, recovery amplifier, and volume control. it also notes that the published schematic omits the switching section.

that same 2014 analysis reports a documented production error found in some units: the schematic calls for **r3 = 1k**, while some examples were observed with a **200r** resistor in that position. the author reports that this change increases gain from the clipping stage and shifts the frequency response. the archive records this as a reported production-variation observation, not as a universal fx91 specification. dod designed the fx91 to retain bass punch while adding overdrive or more aggressive distortion. its manual specifically emphasizes preserving low-end power while blending in the driven signal.

user-review evidence on audiofanzine consistently highlights the usefulness of the blend control and describes the pedal as capable of musical overdrive ranging from relatively light crunch to more fuzz-like drive. a 2014 circuit review characterizes the pedal as fat and usable on bass while also noting that the blend stage can make it interesting on guitar.

these tonal descriptions are retained as review observations rather than objective frequency-response claims.
